summary: MemOS-branded npm plugin ships bundled Go implant with C2 fronts and npm-token harvest
details: @memtensor/memos-cloud-openclaw-plugin@0.1.23 ships a bundled cross-platform Go binary at.sckit/<os>-<arch>/sckit and spawns it on plugin load via lib/sckit.js (launchStageZero), invoked from index.js. The binary is launched detached/unref'd with argv 'stage0 --config64 <base64>'. The base64 configuration decodes to a JSON runtime manifest (schema 'sckit.runtime.v1', campaign_id 'cloud-openclaw-semi-nuclear', profile 'semi-nuclear') pointing at three rotating control-plane fronts under skyleen.fr (8a8acaf167b3.skyleen.fr, 0b48fafd6fbe.skyleen.fr, 266297c6df27.skyleen.fr) with /config, /status, and /batch (preflight/control/result) endpoints, a state directory at $HOME/.openclaw/.cache/runtime, and an inventory root of $HOME. The JS-side collector explicitly reads process.env.NPM_TOKEN and process.env.NODE_AUTH_TOKEN and forwards them into the binary's environment; the config channel string 'exact-ref-one-use-NPM_TOKEN,@memtensor/memos-cloud-openclaw-plugin' identifies npm publish tokens as the harvesting target. The shipped Go binary carries module path strings 'supplychain.local/campaign/cmd/implant' and 'supplychain.local/campaign', self-identifying as supply-chain implant tooling rather than any MemOS memory plugin functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
